title: Chaining with ?
story: You're building a data pipeline: parse raw text into a number, validate it's in range, double it, then check it's even. Any step can fail. With `?`, the entire pipeline is clean — like a domino chain where one fall stops everything.
why: Chaining multiple Result-returning operations with `?` creates clean linear pipelines — each step depends on the previous, and any failure short-circuits the entire chain.
analogy: A pipeline with `?` is like a factory assembly line — each station does its job and passes the product forward. If any station detects a defect, the whole line stops.
try_it: Add a fourth step to `process_number`: check that the number is below 100. Chain it with `?`. What happens when you feed it "50" (even, positive, below 100) vs "102" (all good except below 100)?
tips: Each `?` is a checkpoint — if it fails, execution stops and the error bubbles up
Name your pipeline functions clearly: parse → validate → transform → verify
Keep each step in a pipeline focused on one responsibility — easy to test, easy to reason about
common_mistakes: Writing validation as a separate function but forgetting to call it — the pipeline has gaps
Assuming later steps still run after an earlier `?` fails — they don't, the function already returned
Returning Ok() at every step instead of using `?` — defeats the purpose of short-circuiting
